Surah An-Nahl (al-Nahl, The Bee) [Meccan except the last three verses, which are Medinan; it has 128 verses; it was revealed after Surah al-Kahf]

When the polytheists were slow to receive the punishment, the verse was revealed: ﴿The command of Allah has come, so do not seek to hasten it﴾. That is, the Hour (al-sa'a, the Hour of Resurrection) has come. It is expressed in the past tense (bi-sigha al-madi) to affirm that it will certainly occur; that is, it has drawn near. ﴿So do not seek to hasten it﴾: do not ask for it before its time, for it is certainly going to happen without doubt. ﴿Glory be to Him﴾: exalted above (tanzihan lahu, declaring Him far removed from imperfection). ﴿And exalted is He above what they associate with Him﴾: with other than Him.

Commentary of al-Mahalli and al-Suyuti (Tafsir al-Jalalayn) on surah 16, verse 2:

﴿He sends down the angels﴾, meaning Jibril (Gabriel), ﴿with the Spirit﴾, meaning with the revelation, ﴿by His command﴾, meaning by His will, ﴿upon whomever He wills of His servants﴾, and they are the prophets, ﴿that﴾ (an explanatory *an*, mufassira), ﴿warn﴾, meaning frighten the disbelievers with the punishment and inform them, ﴿that there is no god but I, so fear Me﴾, meaning fear Me.

Commentary of al-Mahalli & al-Suyuti (Tafsir al-Jalalayn) on surah 16, verse 3:

﴿He created the heavens and the earth in truth﴾ i.e., truthfully, ﴿exalted be He above what they associate with Him﴾ of idols.

He created man from a drop of semen (nutfah): (the commentary explains it as) semen, until He made him strong and mighty. ﴿Then behold, he is a contentious adversary.﴾ (The commentary explains: intensely contentious.) ﴿Clear.﴾ (The commentary explains: he made his contention clear in denying the Resurrection, saying: "Who will give life to bones when they are decayed?")

{"Wal-an'am" (the cattle)} — the camels, cows and sheep. It is in the accusative, governed by a verb understood, which the following explains: "He created them for you" — among the people (of the human race). "In them is warmth" — that by which you keep warm, from their hair and wool, such as coverings and cloaks. "And benefits" — from offspring, milk and riding. "And from them you eat" — the prepositional phrase has been placed first for the sake of the rhyme (fasila).

Commentary of al-Mahalli & al-Suyuti (Tafsir al-Jalalayn) on surah 16, verse 6:

﴿And for you in them is beauty﴾ adornment, ﴿when you bring them back (turīhūn)﴾ you return them to their pen (marāḥ) in the evening, ﴿and when you send them out to pasture (tasraḥūn)﴾ you drive them out to the pasture in the morning.

Commentary of al-Mahalli & al-Suyuti (Tafsir al-Jalalayn) on surah 16, verse 7:

﴿And they carry your loads﴾ (aḥmālakum), your burdens, ﴿to a land you could not reach﴾ (wāṣilīna ilayhi), arriving at it, ﴿except with great hardship to yourselves﴾ (bi-jahdihā), by their effort, ﴿without the camels﴾ (ʿalā ghayr al-ibil), ﴿indeed your Lord is Kind and Merciful﴾ (la-raʾūf raḥīm) toward you, in that He created them for you.

And He created the horses, the mules and the donkeys, that you may ride them and as an adornment. (The object of purpose.) The giving of reason for them by [their being] a favour does not preclude their being created for other than that, such as eating [the flesh of] horses, which is established by the hadith in the two Sahihs. ﴿And He creates what you do not know﴾ of wondrous and strange things.

**Commentary of al-Mahalli & al-Suyuti (Tafsir al-Jalalayn) on surah 16, verse 9:**

﴿And upon Allah is the direction of the way﴾, i.e., the explanation of the straight path. ﴿And among them is the deviating﴾, i.e., of the way, ﴿deviating from uprightness﴾. ﴿And had He willed﴾ your guidance ﴿He would have guided you﴾ to the direction of the way ﴿all of you﴾, so that you would be guided to it by your own choice.

Commentary of al-Mahalli & al-Suyuti (Tafsir al-Jalalayn) on surah 16, verse 10:

﴿He it is Who sent down water from the sky; from it you have drink﴾ that you drink, ﴿and from it grows vegetation﴾ that grows by means of it, ﴿in which you pasture your livestock﴾ you graze your animals.

Tafsir al-Jalalayn (Commentary of al-Mahalli and al-Suyuti) on Surah 16, verse 11:

﴿He causes to grow for you thereby the crops, the olives, the palm trees, the grapes, and of all the fruits.﴾ Indeed in that ﴿there is a sign﴾ (ayah), mentioned above, indicating His oneness, exalted be He, ﴿for a people who reflect﴾ upon His creation and so believe.

Commentary of al-Mahalli & al-Suyuti (Tafsir al-Jalalayn) on surah 16, verse 12:

﴿And He subjected for you the night and the day and the sun﴾ — in the accusative, as a conjunction with what precedes it (ʿaṭf); the nominative is also possible, as a new sentence (mubtada᾽). ﴿And the moon and the stars﴾ — with both readings. ﴿Subjected﴾ — in the accusative as a circumstantial state (ḥāl), and in the nominative as a predicate (khabar). ﴿By His command﴾ — by His will. ﴿Indeed in that are signs for a people who reason﴾ — who reflect.

Commentary of al-Mahalli & al-Suyuti (Tafsir al-Jalalayn) on surah 16, verse 13:

﴿And﴾ He subjected for you ﴿what He has created﴾ (i.e., created) ﴿for you on the earth﴾ of animals and plants and other things, ﴿diverse in its colours﴾ such as red, yellow, green and others. ﴿Indeed in that is a sign for a people who take heed﴾ who admonish themselves.

Commentary of al-Mahalli & al-Suyuti (Tafsir al-Jalalayn) on surah 16, verse 14:

﴿And it is He who subjected the sea﴾ made it submissive for riding upon it and diving into it, ﴿that you may eat from it fresh meat﴾ which is fish, ﴿and extract from it ornaments which you wear﴾ which are pearls and coral. ﴿And you see﴾ you behold ﴿the ships﴾ the boats ﴿plowing through it﴾ cleaving the water by their passage through it, advancing and retreating with one wind. ﴿And that you may seek﴾ is coordinated with "that you may eat"; you seek ﴿of His bounty﴾ exalted is He, through trade, ﴿and perhaps you will be grateful﴾ to God for that.

﴿And He cast into the earth firm mountains﴾, mountains that are fixed, ﴿lest it should sway with you﴾, lest it move, ﴿and [He made in it] rivers﴾, like the Nile, ﴿and roads﴾, paths, ﴿so that you may be guided﴾ to your destinations.

Commentary of al-Mahalli & al-Suyuti (Tafsir al-Jalalayn) on surah 16, verse 16:

﴿And landmarks﴾, by which you find your way on the roads, such as the mountains by day, ﴿and by the star﴾, in the sense of the stars, ﴿they find their way﴾ to the roads and the qibla by night.

Commentary of al-Mahalli & al-Suyuti (Tafsir al-Jalalayn) on surah 16, verse 17:

﴿Is He then who creates﴾ being Allah ﴿like one who does not create﴾ being the idols, since you associate them with Him in worship? No! ﴿Will you not then take heed?﴾ of this, so that you would believe.

Commentary of al-Mahalli & al-Suyuti (Tafsir al-Jalalayn) on surah 16, verse 18:

﴿And if you were to count the favour of Allah, you could not enumerate it.﴾ You could not keep count of it, let alone be able to give thanks for it. ﴿Indeed, Allah is Most Forgiving, Most Merciful.﴾ In that He bestows His favours upon you despite your shortcomings and your disobedience.

Commentary of al-Mahalli & al-Suyuti (Tafsir al-Jalalayn) on surah 16, verse 20:

﴿And those whom you invoke﴾ with the ta' and the ya' (i.e., read as tad‘ūna and yad‘ūna), worship ﴿besides Allah﴾, and they are the idols, ﴿who create nothing, and they are created﴾, that is, they are fashioned out of stone and other materials.

Commentary of al-Mahalli & al-Suyuti (Tafsir al-Jalalayn) on surah 16, verse 21:

﴿Dead﴾ (amwat), without spirit in them; a second predicate. ﴿Not living﴾ (ghayr ahya'), an emphasis. ﴿And they do not perceive﴾ (wa ma yash'uruna), i.e., the idols, ﴿when﴾ (ayyana), at what time, ﴿they will be raised﴾ (yub'athuna), i.e., the creation. So how can they be worshipped, since none can be a god except the Creator, the Living, the One who knows the unseen?

Your God is one God. As for those who do not believe in the Hereafter, their hearts deny [the truth], and they are arrogant.

Commentary:

﴿إلَهكُمْ﴾ (Your God): the one who deserves to be worshipped from among you. ﴿إلَه واحِد﴾ (is one God): having no equal in His essence or in His attributes, and He is Allah, exalted is He. ﴿فالَّذِينَ لا يُؤْمِنُونَ بِالآخِرَةِ قُلُوبهمْ مُنْكِرَة﴾ (As for those who do not believe in the Hereafter, their hearts deny): denying, rejecting the Oneness [of God]. ﴿وهُمْ مُسْتَكْبِرُونَ﴾ (and they are arrogant): proud, disdaining to believe in it.

Commentary of al-Mahalli & al-Suyuti (Tafsir al-Jalalayn) on surah 16, verse 23:

﴿Certainly﴾ (ḥaqqan), ﴿that Allah knows what they conceal and what they reveal﴾, so He will recompense them for that. ﴿Indeed, He does not love the arrogant﴾, meaning that He will punish them.

It was revealed concerning al-Nadr ibn al-Harith: ﴿And when it is said to them, "What is it that your Lord has sent down?"﴾ — "what" is interrogative, "that" is a relative pronoun ﴿"What is it that your Lord has sent down?"﴾ — they say: it is ﴿fables of the ancients﴾, lies of the ancients, [said] to mislead the people.

Commentary of al-Mahalli & al-Suyuti (Tafsir al-Jalalayn) on surah 16, verse 25:

﴿That they may bear﴾ in the final outcome of the matter ﴿their burdens in full﴾ their sins, ﴿on the Day of Resurrection, and also some of﴾ the burdens of ﴿those whom they lead astray without knowledge﴾, because they called them to error, so they followed them and thus shared in the sin. ﴿Unquestionably evil is﴾ what is worst, ﴿what they bear﴾ they carry, ﴿this their burden﴾.

Commentary of al-Mahalli & al-Suyuti (Tafsir al-Jalalayn) on surah 16, verse 26:

﴿Indeed, those before them plotted﴾, and they were Nimrod, who built a lofty edifice (ṣarḥ) so that he might ascend from it to the heavens and fight their inhabitants. ﴿Then Allah came upon﴾ (qaṣada, "intended") ﴿their building from its foundations﴾, meaning its base (al-asās). So He sent upon it the wind and the earthquake, and it collapsed. ﴿So the roof fell down upon them from above them﴾, meaning they were beneath it. ﴿And the punishment came to them from where they did not perceive﴾, from a direction that did not occur to them. It is also said that this is a figurative illustration of the undoing of the scheme they had devised against the messengers.

Commentary of al-Mahalli & al-Suyuti (Tafsir al-Jalalayn) on surah 16, verse 27:

﴿Then on the Day of Resurrection He will disgrace them﴾, i.e., humiliate them. ﴿And He will say﴾, God saying to them through the angels, as a rebuke: ﴿"Where are My partners"﴾, according to your claim, ﴿"whom you used to oppose"﴾, i.e., you used to oppose the believers ﴿"concerning them"﴾, concerning their affair? ﴿Those who were given knowledge will say﴾, i.e., will say, from among the prophets and the believers: ﴿"Indeed, disgrace this Day and evil are upon the disbelievers"﴾, saying it in gloating over them.

﴿Those whom the angels take in death﴾, read with the *ta'* (تَتَوَفّاهُمْ) and with the *ya'* (يَتَوَفّاهُمْ), ﴿while they were wronging themselves﴾ by disbelief. ﴿Then they offered submission﴾: they yielded and surrendered at the time of death, saying, ﴿"We did not used to do any evil"﴾, meaning polytheism (*shirk*). Then the angels will say, ﴿"Yes, indeed Allah is Knowing of what you used to do"﴾, so He will recompense you for it.
And it will be said to them: ﴿Enter the gates of Hell, to abide therein forever. How wretched is the abode of the arrogant.﴾ *Mathwa* means *ma'wa* (abode) ﴿of the arrogant﴾.

Commentary of al-Mahalli & al-Suyuti (Tafsir al-Jalalayn) on surah 16, verse 30:

﴿And it will be said to those who were mindful of God﴾ [i.e., those who avoided association with Him (al-shirk)], ﴿"What has your Lord sent down?"﴾ ﴿They will say, "Good."﴾ ﴿For those who did good﴾ [i.e., by faith (bi-l-iman)] ﴿in this world, there is a good [reward]﴾ [i.e., a good life (hayah tayyibah)]. ﴿And the abode of the Hereafter is better﴾ [i.e., Paradise (al-jannah) is better] than the world and what is in it. He, exalted is He, said, ﴿And excellent is the abode of those who are mindful of God,﴾ [meaning] it is [Paradise].

Commentary of al-Mahalli & al-Suyuti (Tafsir al-Jalalayn) on surah 16, verse 31:

﴿Gardens of perpetual residence﴾ (jannāt ʿadn), iqāmah is the subject (mubtada'), its predicate being ﴿they will enter them, rivers flowing beneath them; for them therein is whatever they wish﴾. ﴿Thus﴾ the recompense ﴿Allah rewards the God-fearing﴾.

Commentary of al-Mahalli & al-Suyuti (Tafsir al-Jalalayn) on surah 16, verse 32:

﴿Alladhina﴾ is an attributive (na't) for ﴿those whom the angels take in death while they are pure﴾, meaning purified from disbelief. ﴿They say﴾ to them at the time of death: ﴿Peace be upon you﴾. And it is said to them in the Hereafter: ﴿Enter Paradise for what you used to do﴾.

Commentary of al-Mahalli & al-Suyuti (Tafsir al-Jalalayn) on surah 16, verse 33:

﴿Do they await﴾ (هَلْ يَنْظُرُونَ) — i.e., do the disbelievers await ﴿anything but that the angels come to them﴾ (إلّا أنْ تَأْتِيَهُمُ الْمَلائِكَةُ) — with the verb read with both the ta' and the ya' — ﴿to take their souls﴾ (لِقَبْضِ أرْوَاحِهِمْ), ﴿or that the command of your Lord comes﴾ (أوْ يَأْتِيَ أمْرُ رَبِّكَ) — the punishment, or the Resurrection which encompasses it. ﴿So did those who came before them do﴾ (كَذَلِكَ فَعَلَ الَّذِينَ مِنْ قَبْلِهِمْ) — as these people have done, ﴿of the nations, who denied their messengers and were destroyed.﴾ ﴿And Allah did not wrong them﴾ (وَمَا ظَلَمَهُمُ اللهُ) — by destroying them without a sin — ﴿but they were wronging themselves﴾ (وَلَكِنْ كَانُوا أنْفُسَهُمْ يَظْلِمُونَ) — by disbelief.
﴿So the evils of what they had done afflicted them﴾, i.e., their recompense, ﴿and there descended upon them﴾, i.e., came down upon them, ﴿that at which they used to mock﴾, i.e., the punishment.

Commentary of al-Mahalli & al-Suyuti (Tafsir al-Jalalayn) on surah 16, verse 35:

﴿And those who associated partners with God said﴾ — from among the people of Makkah — ﴿"Had God willed, we would not have worshipped anything apart from Him, neither we nor our fathers, nor would we have made anything unlawful apart from Him"﴾ — [i.e., of the baḥā'ir and sawā'ib (the she-camels and beasts dedicated to idols, which they declared forbidden)]. Our association of partners and our declaring things unlawful is by His will, and so He is pleased with it. ﴿Likewise did those before them act﴾, i.e., they denied their messengers in what they brought. ﴿So is it [upon the messengers] but to deliver the clear message?﴾ — i.e., what is upon the messengers is nothing but the plain delivery, and it is not incumbent upon them to guide.

Commentary of al-Mahalli & al-Suyuti (Tafsir al-Jalalayn) on surah 16, verse 36:

﴿And We certainly sent into every nation a messenger﴾ as We sent you to these people, ﴿saying﴾ i.e., with the message: ﴿"Worship Allah"﴾ make Him one, ﴿and avoid the Taghut﴾ the idols, by not worshipping them. ﴿Then among them were those whom Allah guided﴾ so they believed, ﴿and among them were those upon whom error was justly due﴾ it was decreed, ﴿in Allah's knowledge, so they did not believe. ﴿So travel through the earth and observe how was the end of the deniers﴾ their messengers, of destruction.

﴿If you, O Muhammad, are eager for their guidance﴾, though God has led them astray, you cannot achieve that. ﴿Indeed God does not guide﴾ (read with the verb in the passive, *yuhda*, and in the active, *yahdi*) ﴿those whom He causes to go astray﴾, meaning those whom He intends to lead astray. ﴿And they will have no helpers﴾, no protectors who can keep them from the punishment of God.

They swore by God with their most earnest oaths. [Jalalayn: "with their most earnest oaths", i.e. the utmost of their effort in them.] God says: ﴿Yes, [He will resurrect them]﴾ [as] a promise ﴿binding upon Him, a truth﴾. Both are verbal nouns (masdar) emphasizing their verb, in the accusative, governed by their implied verb, meaning: He promised that and made it true, a truth. ﴿But most of mankind﴾ [i.e. the people of Makkah] ﴿do not know﴾ that.

The phrase ﴿li-yubayyina﴾ (that He may make clear) is connected to the implied verb ﴿yab'athuhum﴾ (He will resurrect them), which is understood here though not stated. ﴿Lahum alladhi yakhtalifuna﴾ means "for them that about which they differ" with the believers, ﴿fihi﴾ (concerning it) refers to the matter of religion, namely their punishment and the reward of the believers. ﴿Wa-li-ya'lama alladhina kafaru annahum kanu kadhibin﴾ means "and that those who disbelieved may know that they were liars" in denying the resurrection.

Tafsir al-Jalalayn (al-Mahalli and al-Suyuti) on Surah 16, verse 40:

﴿Indeed, Our word to a thing when We intend it is only that We say to it, "Be," and it is.﴾ That is, when We intend its bringing into existence. "Our word" (qawluna) is the subject (mubtada'), and its predicate (khabar) is ﴿that We say to it, "Be," and it is.﴾ That is, it is (fa-huwa yakun), i.e. it comes to be. In another reading it is in the accusative (bil-nasb), coordinated (ʿatfan) upon "naqul" (We say). The verse serves to establish the power to resurrect (taqrir al-qudra ʿala al-ba'th).

Commentary of al-Mahalli & al-Suyuti (Tafsir al-Jalalayn) on surah 16, verse 41:

﴿Those who emigrated for the sake of Allah﴾ to establish His religion, ﴿after they had been wronged﴾ with harm from the people of Makkah, namely the Prophet (ﷺ) and his Companions, ﴿We will surely settle them﴾ We will lodge them ﴿in this world in a good dwelling﴾ which is Madinah, ﴿and the reward of the Hereafter is greater﴾ i.e., Paradise is greater, ﴿if only they knew﴾ i.e., the disbelievers or those who stayed behind from the emigration, what honour the emigrants have, they would have joined them.

They are ﴿those who were patient﴾ in enduring the harm of the polytheists and in emigrating (al-hijra) to make the religion manifest, ﴿and upon their Lord they rely﴾, so He provides for them from where they do not expect.

Commentary of al-Mahalli & al-Suyuti (Tafsir al-Jalalayn) on surah 16, verse 43:

﴿And We did not send before you except men to whom We revealed⁠—﴾ not angels. ﴿So ask the people of the reminder⁠﴾ the scholars of the Torah and the Gospel ﴿if you do not know﴾ that. ﴿For they know it, and you are closer to believing them than the believers in Muhammad (ﷺ)⁠﴾

Commentary of al-Mahalli & al-Suyuti (Tafsir al-Jalalayn) on surah 16, verse 44:

﴿With the clear proofs﴾ is related to something omitted, i.e., We sent them with the clear proofs. ﴿And the scriptures﴾ means the books. ﴿And We have sent down to you the Reminder﴾ means the Qur'an, ﴿that you may explain to mankind what has been sent down to them﴾ in it of the lawful and the unlawful, ﴿and that they may give thought﴾ about that, ﴿so that they may take heed﴾.

Commentary of al-Mahalli & al-Suyuti (Tafsir al-Jalalayn) on surah 16, verse 45:

﴿Do those who devised evil plots (al-makrat al-sayyi'at, i.e., the evil schemes) feel secure⁠—﴾ against the Prophet ﷺ in the Dar al-Nadwa (the council house of the Quraysh), from restraining him, or killing him, or expelling him, as mentioned in Surat al-Anfal ﴿that God will cause the earth to swallow them up,﴾ like Qarun ﴿or that the punishment will come upon them from a direction they do not perceive﴾, i.e., from a direction that does not occur to their minds. They were destroyed at Badr, and they were not expecting that.

Commentary of al-Mahalli & al-Suyuti (Tafsir al-Jalalayn) on surah 16, verse 46:

﴿Or He seizes them in their going to and fro,﴾ in their journeys for trade, ﴿and they cannot escape Him.﴾ They cannot escape the punishment.

﴿Or He seizes them by gradual decline﴾: [He] reduces [them] little by little until they all perish. *Ḥāl* (a circumstantial qualifier, describing the state of the subject or object) is in the accusative, referring to either the agent or the object. ﴿Indeed your Lord is Most Kind, Most Merciful﴾, in that He did not hasten the punishment against them.

Commentary of al-Mahalli & al-Suyuti (Tafsir al-Jalalayn) on surah 16, verse 48:

﴿Have they not considered what things Allah has created, whose shadows incline to the right and to the left, prostrating to Allah, and they are humbled?﴾ Anything that has a shadow, such as a tree or a mountain. ﴿Its shadows incline﴾ they turn, ﴿from the right and the left﴾ plural of shimal (left), meaning from both its sides, in the morning and in the evening. ﴿Prostrating to Allah﴾ a circumstantial clause (hal), meaning submissive to Him in whatever is required of them. ﴿While they are humbled﴾ i.e., the shadows, ﴿daakhiroon﴾ abased, lowly. They were treated as rational beings.

Commentary of al-Mahalli & al-Suyuti (Tafsir al-Jalalayn) on surah 16, verse 49:

﴿And to Allah prostrates whatever is in the heavens and whatever is on the earth of creature [that moves on it]﴾, i.e., soul (nasamah) that crawls upon it, i.e., submits to Him by what is intended of it; and the usage (al-ityan) of [the plural form for] that which does not reason (ma la ya'qil) predominated because of its abundance. ﴿And the angels﴾, He singled them out for mention as a mark of their excellence. ﴿And they are not arrogant﴾, they do not become proud (yatakabbarun) to refuse His worship.

"They fear" — i.e., the angels — is a circumstantial clause (ḥāl) relating to the pronoun in "they are arrogant." "Their Lord from above them" is a circumstantial clause relating to "them," meaning: exalted over them with dominance (al-qahr). "And they do what they are commanded" — i.e., to do.

Commentary of al-Mahalli & al-Suyuti (Tafsir al-Jalalayn) on surah 16, verse 51:

﴿And Allah said: Do not take two gods. ﴾ (This is) emphasis. ﴿He is only one God.﴾ He brought it to establish the divinity and the oneness. ﴿So fear Me, and Me alone.﴾ Fear Me (ارهبون, "fear") rather than other than Me. And in it is a shift (iltifat, a change of grammatical person) from the third person (al-ghaybah, absence).

Commentary of al-Mahalli & al-Suyuti (Tafsir al-Jalalayn) on surah 16, verse 52:

﴿To Him belongs whatever is in the heavens and the earth﴾, in ownership, creation and servitude. ﴿And to Him is the religion﴾, meaning obedience, ﴿perpetual﴾, meaning constant. It is a circumstantial clause (hal) relating to "the religion," and the governing element within it carries the sense of an adverbial of time (zarf). ﴿Is it other than Allah you fear?﴾ He is the true God, and there is no god but Him. The interrogative is for denunciation and reproach.

Commentary of al-Mahalli & al-Suyuti (Tafsir al-Jalalayn) on surah 16, verse 53:

﴿Whatever blessing you have is from Allah.﴾ It does not come except from Him, and "mā" (whatever) is either a conditional particle or a relative pronoun. ﴿Then when harm touches you﴾ afflicts you, ﴿the adversity﴾ poverty and sickness, ﴿to Him you cry aloud﴾ you raise your voices in supplication and calling upon Him for help, and you do not call upon anyone other than Him.

Commentary of al-Mahalli & al-Suyuti (Tafsir al-Jalalayn) on surah 16, verse 55:

﴿So that they may deny what We have given them﴾ of blessing, ﴿so enjoy yourselves﴾ by your gathering together in the worship of idols. It is a command of threat. ﴿But you will come to know﴾ the outcome of that.

Commentary of al-Mahalli & al-Suyuti (Tafsir al-Jalalayn) on surah 16, verse 56:

﴿And they assign﴾ i.e., the polytheists, ﴿to that which they do not know﴾ that it harms and does not benefit, namely the idols, ﴿a share of what We have provided them﴾ of the tilth and the cattle, by their saying: "This is for God, and this is for our associates." ﴿By God, you will certainly be questioned﴾ a questioning of rebuke, and in it there is a shift (iltifat) from the third person (ghaybah) [to the second person], ﴿about what you used to fabricate﴾ against God, namely that He commanded you to do that.

Commentary of al-Mahalli and al-Suyuti (Tafsir al-Jalalayn) on surah 16, verse 57:

﴿They attribute daughters to Allah﴾, by their saying that the angels are the daughters of Allah. ﴿Glory be to Him﴾, exalting Him above what they claim. ﴿And for themselves what they desire﴾, that is, sons. The clause is in a position of raf' (nominative) or nasb (accusative) with yaj'alūn ("they attribute"). The meaning is: they attribute to Him the daughters, which they themselves dislike, while He is exempt from having offspring. And they attribute to themselves the sons whom they choose, so they reserve for themselves the most excellent. This is like His saying: ﴿So ask them: Has your Lord daughters while they have sons?﴾

Commentary of al-Mahalli & al-Suyuti (Tafsir al-Jalalayn) on surah 16, verse 58:

﴿When one of them is given the good news of a female (child), his face becomes darkened (ẓalla), i.e., it became (ṣāra) (wajhuhu muswaddan), i.e., changed in the manner of one who is distressed, ﴿and he is suppressed with grief﴾, i.e., filled with grief. How, then, can daughters be attributed to Him, exalted is He?﴾

Commentary of al-Mahalli & al-Suyuti (Tafsir al-Jalalayn) on surah 16, verse 59:

﴿Yatawārā﴾ (he hides himself) yakhtafī (he conceals himself) ﴿min al-qawm﴾ (from the people), i.e., his people, ﴿min sū' mā bushshira bihi﴾ (because of the evil of that of which he was given good news), out of fear of reproach, ﴿mutaraddidan fīmā yaf'alu bihi﴾ (hesitating over what he should do with it), ﴿a-yumsikuhu﴾ (whether he should keep it) yatrukuhu (leave it) bilā qatl (without killing it) ﴿ʿalā hūn﴾ (in humiliation) hawān (disgrace) wa dhull (and abasement), ﴿am yadussuhu fī al-turāb﴾ (or bury it in the dust) bi-an ya'iddahu (by burying it alive), ﴿alā sā'a﴾ (unquestionably evil is) bi'sa (what) ﴿mā yaḥkumūn﴾ (they judge). Their judgment, that is, in that they attributed to their Creator daughters, who are with them in this place (i.e., they consider them a disgrace).

Commentary of al-Mahalli & al-Suyuti (Tafsir al-Jalalayn) on surah 16, verse 60:

﴿For those who do not believe in the Hereafter﴾, i.e., the disbelievers, ﴿is the evil similitude﴾, i.e., the evil attribute (al-sawʾa, meaning "the ugly one"), which is their burying of daughters alive, despite their need of them for marriage. ﴿And to Allah belongs the highest similitude﴾, i.e., the highest attribute, which is that there is no god but Him. ﴿And He is the Mighty﴾ in His dominion, ﴿the Wise﴾ in His creation.

Commentary of al-Mahalli & al-Suyuti (Tafsir al-Jalalayn) on surah 16, verse 61:

﴿And if Allah were to seize mankind for their wrongdoing﴾ by their sins, ﴿He would not leave upon it﴾ i.e., the earth, ﴿any creature﴾ a living soul that moves upon it, ﴿but He defers them to a specified term. And when their term comes, they will not remain behind it﴾ from it ﴿an hour, nor will they precede it﴾ upon it.

**Commentary of al-Mahalli and al-Suyuti (Tafsir al-Jalalayn) on Surah 16, verse 62:**

﴿And they attribute to Allah what they dislike﴾ for themselves: daughters, and a partner in leadership, and the humiliation of the messengers. ﴿And their tongues describe﴾ (i.e., say) ﴿alongside that the lie﴾, which is ﴿that for them is the best (al-ḥusnā)﴾ with Allah, meaning Paradise, in accordance with His saying: ﴿And if I am returned to my Lord, indeed I shall have with Him the best (al-ḥusnā)﴾. ﴿Undoubtedly (lā jaram)﴾, truly, ﴿for them is the Fire, and they are ﴿mufraṭūn﴾﴾ (meaning) abandoned therein, or sent forward to it. In another recitation (qirā'a), with the letter rā' pronounced with a kasra (mufriḍūn), meaning those who exceed the limit.

By Allah, We certainly sent messengers to nations before you, but Satan made their deeds appear attractive to them, so he became their patron today (i.e., in this world), and for them there is a painful punishment (painful: causing pain) in the Hereafter. It has been said that "today" refers to the Day of Resurrection, in the sense of narrating a future situation: meaning, they will have no patron other than him, and he is powerless to help himself, so how could he help them?

Commentary of al-Mahalli & al-Suyuti (Tafsir al-Jalalayn) on surah 16, verse 64:

﴿And We did not send down to you, O Muhammad, the Book﴾ the Qur'an ﴿except that you may make clear to them that about which they differ﴾ concerning matters of the religion, ﴿and as guidance﴾ a conjunction with "that you may make clear" ﴿and mercy for a people who believe﴾ in it.

And Allah sends down water from the sky, and with it gives life to the earth ﴿with vegetation﴾ ﴿after its death﴾, its dryness. ﴿Indeed, in that﴾ mentioned [matter] ﴿is surely a sign﴾ indicating the resurrection ﴿for a people who listen﴾, listening with contemplation.

Commentary of al-Mahalli & al-Suyuti (Tafsir al-Jalalayn) on surah 16, verse 66:

﴿And indeed, for you in the cattle there is a lesson﴾ (i'tibar, reflection) ﴿We give you to drink﴾ (a clarification of the lesson) ﴿of what is in their bellies﴾ (i.e., the cattle), ﴿from﴾ (min, here denoting the starting point, connected with "We give you to drink"), ﴿between dung﴾ (the residue of the rumen) ﴿and blood, pure milk﴾ (unmixed with anything of the dung or blood, whether in taste, smell, colour, or any combination of these), ﴿palatable to the drinkers﴾ (easy to pass down their throats, not causing choking).

And of the fruits of the date-palms and grapevines, [you derive] intoxicant (sakaran) and good provision (rizqan hasanan). The intoxicant is wine (khamran) that intoxicates; it was named by the verbal noun (sukr being the verbal noun, used for the thing itself). This was before its prohibition. [The good provision is] such as dates, raisins, vinegar and date-syrup. Indeed in that, the aforementioned, is a sign (ayah) indicating His power, the Exalted, for a people who reflect (ya'qilun), i.e., who ponder (yatadabbarun).

Commentary of al-Mahalli & al-Suyuti (Tafsir al-Jalalayn) on surah 16, verse 68:

﴿And your Lord inspired to the bee﴾: inspiration of instinct (waḥy ilhām). ﴿That﴾: it is either explanatory (mufassira) or verbal-source (maṣdariyya). ﴿Take for yourselves houses in the mountains﴾ in which you dwell, ﴿and in the trees﴾ houses, ﴿and in what they erect﴾, i.e., what people build for you from places; otherwise you would not dwell in them.

Commentary of al-Mahalli & al-Suyuti (Tafsir al-Jalalayn) on surah 16, verse 69:

﴿Then eat from all the fruits, and go along the ways of your Lord, made easy.﴾ Enter ﴿the ways of your Lord﴾, its paths in seeking pasture, ﴿made easy﴾: the plural of dhalul (docile), a circumstantial state (hal) of "the ways", meaning: subjugated for you, so they are not difficult for you even if they are rugged, and you will not go astray in returning from them even if they are far. It was also said that it is from the pronoun in "go along" (uslukī), meaning: submissive to what is required of you. ﴿From their bellies there comes forth a drink﴾, which is honey, ﴿of varying colours, in which is healing for mankind﴾ from ailments. It was said that it is a healing for some of them, as the indefiniteness of "healing" indicates, or for all of them when it is combined with other things, and without them by intention. The Prophet (ﷺ) ordered it for the one whose belly had been loosened, as related by al-Shaykhan (al-Bukhari and Muslim). ﴿Indeed in that is a sign for a people who give thought﴾ to His creation, exalted is He.

﴿And Allah created you﴾ when you were nothing. ﴿Then He causes you to die﴾ when your appointed terms come to an end. ﴿And among you is one who is returned to the most abject age﴾, meaning the most degraded part of life, through senility (haram) and dotage (kharaf). ﴿So that he knows nothing after having known﴾. Ikrimah said: whoever recites the Qur'an will not reach this state. ﴿Indeed, Allah is All-Knowing﴾ of the arrangement of His creation, ﴿All-Powerful﴾ over whatever He wills.

Commentary of al-Mahalli and al-Suyuti (Tafsir al-Jalalayn) on surah 16, verse 71:

﴿And Allah has favoured some of you over others in provision.﴾ So among you are the wealthy and the poor, the owners and the owned. ﴿Yet those who have been favoured﴾, that is, the masters (al-mawali), ﴿do not give over their provision to what their right hands possess﴾, that is, they do not make what We have provided them of wealth and other things a partnership between themselves and their slaves. ﴿So they are equal in it﴾, that is, the slaves and the masters are partners. The meaning is: they have no partners among their slaves in their wealth. So how do they make some of Allah's slaves partners with Him? ﴿Then do they deny the favour of Allah?﴾ That is, they disbelieve, by making partners with Him.

Commentary of al-Mahalli & al-Suyuti (Tafsir al-Jalalayn) on surah 16, verse 72:

﴿And Allah made for you, from yourselves, spouses﴾ — so He created Hawwa' (Eve) from the rib of Adam, and the rest of mankind from the sperm-drops of men and women. ﴿And made for you, from your spouses, sons and grandchildren﴾ — the children of the children. ﴿And provided for you of the good things﴾ — of the various kinds of fruits, grains and livestock. ﴿Then in falsehood﴾ — the idol — ﴿do they believe, and in the favour of Allah do they disbelieve?﴾ — by their associating others with Him.

﴿And they worship besides Allah﴾, i.e., other than Him, ﴿that which does not possess for them any provision from the heavens﴾ by way of rain, ﴿and the earth﴾ by way of plants, ﴿any﴾ "شَيْئًا", which is a *badal* (substitute, in grammatical apposition) of "رِزْقًا" (provision), ﴿nor are they able﴾, i.e., they have no power over anything. This refers to the idols.

Commentary of al-Mahalli & al-Suyuti (Tafsir al-Jalalayn) on surah 16, verse 74:

﴿So do not coin similitudes for Allah﴾ — do not make for Allah likenesses that you associate with Him, ﴿Indeed, Allah knows﴾ that He has no like, ﴿while you do not know﴾ that.

God struck an example: [a slave (ʿabdan) — a substitute (badal) for "an example"] — "a slave owned (mamlūkan)," a qualifier that distinguishes him from the free man, for he is a servant of God — "who has no power over anything," because he owns nothing. "And one" — an indefinite noun qualified (naksira mawṣūfa), meaning "a free man" — "whom We have provided with good provision from Us, so he spends from it secretly and openly," i.e., he disposes of it as he wishes. The first is the example of the idols, and the second is the example of Him, exalted is He.

"Are they equal?" — i.e., the impotent slaves and the free man who disposes of his wealth? No. "Praise be to God" — alone. "But most of them" — i.e., the people of Makkah — "do not know" what punishment they are heading toward, and so they associate partners with Him.

God sets forth an example (﴿وضَرَبَ اللَّه مَثَلًا﴾), which is in apposition to it: two men (﴿رَجُلَيْنِ﴾), one of them mute (﴿أحَدهما أبْكَم﴾), born deaf and dumb, (﴿لا يَقْدِر عَلى شَيْء﴾) unable to do anything, because he neither understands nor makes himself understood. (﴿وهُوَ كَلٌّ﴾) He is a burden (ثَقِيل) upon (﴿عَلى مَوْلاهُ﴾) his master, the one responsible for his affairs, (﴿أيْنَما يُوَجِّههُ﴾) wherever he directs him, (يَصْرِفهُ) turns him about, (﴿لا يَأْتِ﴾) he does not bring (﴿مِنهُ﴾ from him) (﴿بِخَيْرٍ﴾) any good, (يَنْجَح) he does not succeed. This is the example of the disbeliever.

(﴿هَلْ يَسْتَوِي هُوَ﴾) Are they equal? That is, the mute man mentioned, (﴿ومَن يَأْمُر بِالعَدْلِ﴾) and the one who commands justice, (أيْ ومَن هُوَ ناطِق نافِع لِلنّاسِ حَيْثُ يَأْمُر بِهِ ويَحُثّ عَلَيْهِ) that is, one who speaks and benefits people by commanding justice and urging it, (﴿وهُوَ عَلى صِراط﴾ a path) (﴿مُسْتَقِيم﴾) that is straight, (وهُوَ الثّانِي المُؤْمِن؟ لا) and he is the second, the believer? No. (وقِيلَ هَذا مَثَل اللَّهِ والأَبْكَمُ لِلْأَصْنامِ والَّذِي قَبْله مَثَل الكافِر والمُؤْمِن) It has also been said that this is an example of God and the mute is an example of the idols, while the one before it is an example of the disbeliever and the believer.

Commentary of al-Mahalli & al-Suyuti (Tafsir al-Jalalayn) on surah 16, verse 77:

﴿And to Allah belongs the unseen of the heavens and the earth﴾, i.e., the knowledge of what is hidden in them. ﴿And the matter of the Hour is not but as a glance of the eye or even nearer﴾, because it occurs by the word "Be," and it is.

Commentary of al-Mahalli & al-Suyuti (Tafsir al-Jalalayn) on surah 16, verse 78:

﴿And Allah brought you forth from the wombs of your mothers, knowing nothing﴾. The clause is a circumstantial clause (ḥāl).
﴿And He made for you hearing﴾, with the meaning of "hearings" (al-asmāʿ),
﴿and sight and hearts﴾, meaning the hearts (al-qulūb).
﴿So that you may be grateful﴾, that is, that you may thank Him for that, and thus believe.

Commentary of al-Mahalli & al-Suyuti (Tafsir al-Jalalayn) on surah 16, verse 79:

﴿Have they not considered the birds, made subservient in the air of the sky?﴾ Made subservient (muzallalat) for flight. ﴿In the air of the sky﴾, i.e., the atmosphere between the sky and the earth. ﴿None holds them up﴾ when they fold or spread their wings, so that they fall, ﴿except Allah﴾ by His power. ﴿Surely in that are signs for a people who believe﴾. He created them such that flight is possible for them, and He created the air such that flight in it and their being held up is possible.

Commentary of al-Mahalli & al-Suyuti (Tafsir al-Jalalayn) on surah 16, verse 80:

﴿And Allah has made for you, from your houses, a dwelling﴾ (sakan), a place in which you reside. ﴿And He has made for you, from the hides of cattle, houses﴾ such as tents and domes, ﴿which you find light to carry﴾ for transport, ﴿on the day of your travel﴾ (za'n), your journey, ﴿and on the day of your settling down. And from their wool﴾ i.e., of sheep, ﴿and their fur﴾ i.e., of camels, ﴿and their hair﴾ i.e., of goats, ﴿are furnishings﴾ (athath), goods for your houses, such as carpets and coverings, ﴿and provision﴾ that you enjoy, ﴿for a time﴾ in which it wears out.

﴿And Allah has made for you, from what He has created,﴾ [shade] from the houses, the trees and the clouds, ﴿shade﴾, the plural of ظِلّ (ẓill), which protects you from the heat of the sun. ﴿And He has made for you, from the mountains, shelters﴾, the plural of كِنّ (kinn), which is that in which one takes shelter, such as caves and hollows. ﴿And He has made for you garments﴾, meaning shirts, ﴿which protect you from the heat﴾, i.e., and the cold. ﴿And garments which protect you from your violence﴾, meaning your warfare, i.e., thrusting and striking within them, like coats of mail and padded armour. ﴿Thus﴾, as He created these things, ﴿He completes His favour﴾ in this world ﴿upon you﴾ by creating what you need. ﴿That you may﴾, O people of Makkah, ﴿submit﴾, meaning, that you may affirm His oneness.

Commentary of al-Mahalli & al-Suyuti (Tafsir al-Jalalayn) on surah 16, verse 82:

﴿Then if they turn away﴾ from Islam, ﴿then upon you [O Muhammad] is only the clear conveyance﴾ the plain delivery [of the message]. This was before the command to fight.

Commentary of al-Mahalli & al-Suyuti (Tafsir al-Jalalayn) on surah 16, verse 83:

﴿They recognise the favour of Allah﴾, i.e., they acknowledge that it is from Him, ﴿then they deny it﴾ by their associating others with Him.

Commentary of al-Mahalli & al-Suyuti (Tafsir al-Jalalayn) on surah 16, verse 84:

﴿And﴾ mention ﴿the Day We raise up from every nation a witness﴾. He is their prophet, who bears witness for them and against them, and this is the Day of Resurrection. ﴿Then, those who disbelieved will not be permitted﴾ to offer excuses, ﴿nor will they be asked to make amends﴾. It is not demanded of them al-ʿutbā (the returning to what pleases God), i.e., the return to what pleases Allah.
And when those who wronged [i.e., disbelieved] see the punishment [i.e., the Fire], it will not be lightened for them, nor will they be reprieved from it when they see it.

**Commentary of al-Mahalli & al-Suyuti (Tafsir al-Jalalayn) on surah 16, verse 86:**

﴿When those who associated partners [with Allah] see their partners,﴾ from among the devils and others, ﴿they will say, "Our Lord, these are our partners whom we used to invoke﴾ worship ﴿besides You." But they will cast at them the saying﴾ i.e., they will say to them ﴿"Indeed, you are liars,"﴾ in your claim that you were worshipping us, as in another verse, ﴿"They did not worship us."﴾ They will disown their worship.

Commentary of al-Mahalli & al-Suyuti (Tafsir al-Jalalayn) on surah 16, verse 87:

﴿And they will submit to Allah on that Day, and that which they used to invent will fail them.﴾ That is, they submitted to His judgment. ﴿And there will be lost to them﴾ that is, there will be absent from them ﴿what they used to invent﴾ of the claim that their gods would intercede for them.

Commentary of al-Mahalli & al-Suyuti (Tafsir al-Jalalayn) on surah 16, verse 88:

﴿Those who disbelieved and barred⦆ people ﴿from the way of Allah﴾ meaning His religion, ﴿We shall increase them in punishment upon punishment﴾ which they deserved because of their disbelief. Ibn Mas'ud said: [they are] scorpions whose fangs are like tall palm trees. ﴿Because they used to spread corruption﴾ by their barring people from faith.

Commentary of al-Mahalli & al-Suyuti (Tafsir al-Jalalayn) on surah 16, verse 89:

﴿And﴾ mention ﴿the Day We raise up in every nation a witness against them from among themselves﴾, who is their prophet, ﴿and We bring you, O Muhammad, as a witness against these﴾, i.e., your people, ﴿and We have sent down to you the Book﴾, the Qur'an, ﴿as an explanation﴾, a clarification ﴿of all things﴾ that people need concerning the matters of the Sharia (divine law), ﴿and as guidance﴾ from misguidance, ﴿and mercy and good tidings﴾ of Paradise ﴿for the Muslims﴾, those who affirm the oneness of God.

Commentary of al-Mahalli & al-Suyuti (Tafsir al-Jalalayn) on surah 16, verse 90:

﴿Indeed, Allah commands justice﴾ (al-'adl), meaning tawhid (affirmation of the Oneness of God) or equity (al-insaf), ﴿and beneficence﴾ (al-ihsan), meaning performing the obligations (al-fara'id), or that you worship Allah as if you see Him, as in the hadith, ﴿and giving to the near of kin﴾ (dhi al-qurba), meaning giving to relatives. He singled it out for mention out of concern for it. ﴿And He forbids immorality﴾ (al-fahsha'), meaning fornication (al-zina), ﴿and wrongdoing﴾ (al-munkar), meaning what is disapproved by the Law, of disbelief and acts of disobedience, ﴿and oppression﴾ (al-baghy), meaning wronging people. He singled it out for mention out of concern for it, just as He began with immorality, likewise. ﴿He admonishes you﴾ through the commands and prohibitions, ﴿that you may remember﴾, meaning that you may take heed. In this there is an idgham (assimilation) of the ta' of the original root into the dhal. And in al-Mustadrak, from Ibn Mas'ud, it is said: this is the most comprehensive verse in the Qur'an for good and evil.

Commentary of al-Mahalli & al-Suyuti (Tafsir al-Jalalayn) on surah 16, verse 91:

﴿And fulfil the covenant of Allah when you have covenanted﴾, [i.e., the covenants of] sales, oaths and other things; ﴿and do not break the oaths after their confirmation﴾, after their affirmation (tawthiq); ﴿and you have made Allah your surety﴾, guaranteeing the fulfilment, when you swore by Him; and the clause is a circumstantial (ḥāl) clause; ﴿indeed Allah knows what you do﴾, a warning to them.

Commentary of al-Mahalli & al-Suyuti (Tafsir al-Jalalayn) on surah 16, verse 92:

﴿And do not be like her who unravels﴾ undoes, ﴿her spun thread﴾ what she has spun, ﴿after it has been [well] made strong﴾ after its strengthening and twisting, ﴿into fragments﴾ a circumstantial state, plural of nakth, which is what is unraveled, i.e., its strength is undone. She was a foolish woman from Makkah who used to spin all day and then unravel it. ﴿You take﴾ a circumstantial clause referring to the pronoun in "do not be": i.e., do not be like her in your taking ﴿your oaths as [means of] deception﴾ dakhal, which is what enters into a thing without being part of it, i.e., corruption or treachery ﴿between you﴾ by breaking them ﴿because﴾ i.e., because ﴿one community is greater﴾ more numerous ﴿than another community.﴾ They used to make alliances with allies, and when they found a group more numerous and more powerful than them, they would break the alliance with those and ally with them instead. ﴿Indeed, Allah only tests you thereby﴾ tests you ﴿with it﴾, i.e., with what He has commanded regarding fulfilling the covenant, so that He may see who among you is obedient and who is disobedient, or [with] "one community being greater," so that He may see whether you fulfil or not. ﴿And He will surely make clear to you on the Day of Resurrection that over which you used to differ﴾ in the worldly life, concerning the matter of the covenant and other things, by punishing the one who breaks it and rewarding the one who fulfils it.

﴿And if God had willed, He would have made you one community﴾, people of one religion, ﴿but He leads astray whom He wills and guides whom He wills. You will surely be questioned﴾ on the Day of Resurrection with a question of rebuke (*tabkit*), ﴿about what you used to do﴾, so that you may be recompensed for it.

Commentary of al-Mahalli & al-Suyuti (Tafsir al-Jalalayn) on surah 16, verse 94:

﴿And do not take your oaths as a means of deceit among yourselves﴾ (he repeated it for emphasis). ﴿Lest a foot slip﴾ after being firm, i.e., your feet slip away from the clear path of Islam ﴿after its firmness﴾, its being steadfast upon it. ﴿And you taste the evil﴾, i.e., the punishment, ﴿for what you have averted from the way of Allah﴾, i.e., because of your averting yourselves from fulfilling the covenant, or your averting others from it, since they follow your example. ﴿And for you there is a great punishment﴾ in the Hereafter.

"Do not sell the covenant of God for a small price" — [that is, of worldly goods], by breaking it for its sake. "What is with God," of reward, "is better for you," than what is in the world, "if you but knew" that, so do not break it.

Commentary of al-Mahalli & al-Suyuti (Tafsir al-Jalalayn) on surah 16, verse 96:

﴿What is with you﴾ of the world ﴿will come to an end﴾, it will perish; ﴿but what is with Allah is lasting﴾, enduring. ﴿And We will surely reward﴾ (read with the ya' and the nun) ﴿those who were patient﴾ in fulfilling the covenants ﴿with the best of what they used to do﴾, "best" here meaning "good."

Commentary of al-Mahalli & al-Suyuti (Tafsir al-Jalalayn) on surah 16, verse 97:

﴿Whoever does righteousness, whether male or female, while being a believer – We will surely cause him to live a good life.﴾ It is said: it is the life of Paradise. And it is said: in this world, through contentment (qana'ah) or lawful provision (rizq halal).

Commentary of al-Mahalli & al-Suyuti (Tafsir al-Jalalayn) on surah 16, verse 98:

﴿When you recite the Qur'an﴾, i.e., intend to recite it, ﴿then seek refuge in Allah from the accursed Satan﴾, i.e., say: "I seek refuge in Allah from the accursed Satan."
﴿Indeed, he has no authority over them﴾ — tasallut (dominion, power over them).

Commentary of al-Mahalli & al-Suyuti (Tafsir al-Jalalayn) on surah 16, verse 100:

﴿Indeed, his authority is only over those who take him as an ally﴾ by obeying him, ﴿and those who associate others with Him﴾ — i.e., with Allah.

Tafsir al-Jalalayn (al-Mahalli and al-Suyuti) on Surah 16, verse 101:

﴿And when We substitute one verse in place of another﴾ by abrogating it (naskh) and sending down another in its place, for the benefit of the servants, ﴿and Allah knows best what He sends down, they say﴾ i.e., the disbelievers say to the Prophet (ﷺ), ﴿"You are only a fabricator"﴾ a liar, who says it of his own accord, ﴿but most of them do not know﴾ the reality of the Qur'an and the benefit of abrogation (naskh).

﴿Say﴾ to them, ﴿"It was sent down by the Holy Spirit"﴾ (Jibril) ﴿"from your Lord in truth"﴾. The phrase ﴿بِالحَقِّ﴾ (bil-haqq, "in truth") is grammatically dependent on the verb ﴿نَزَّلَ﴾ (nazzala, "sent down"). ﴿"So that He may make firm those who believe"﴾ in their faith in it.

Translation:

﴿And indeed﴾ [the particle] "wa-laqad" is for emphasis. ﴿We know that they say, "Only a human teaches him"﴾ [i.e., the Qur'an] ﴿a human being﴾, and he was a Christian smith (qayn) who used to visit the Prophet ﷺ. ﴿The tongue﴾ [i.e., the language] ﴿of the one they incline toward﴾ [i.e., they incline toward it, claiming] that he teaches him ﴿is foreign﴾ (a'jamiyy), ﴿while this﴾ Qur'an ﴿is in a clear Arabic tongue﴾, possessing clarity and eloquence. How then could a foreigner be teaching him?

Commentary of al-Mahalli & al-Suyuti (Tafsir al-Jalalayn) on surah 16, verse 104:

﴿Indeed, those who do not believe in the signs of Allah – Allah will not guide them, and for them is a painful punishment.﴾ (مُؤْلِم) painful

Commentary of al-Mahalli & al-Suyuti (Tafsir al-Jalalayn) on surah 16, verse 105:

﴿Only those fabricate lies who do not believe in the signs of Allah﴾ — the Qur'an — by their saying this is merely the word of a human being. ﴿And it is they who are the liars.﴾ The emphasis by repetition (the repeated "they"/"they are") and by inna (indeed) and other such particles is a rebuttal of their statement: ﴿You are only a fabricator.﴾

Commentary of al-Mahalli & al-Suyuti (Tafsir al-Jalalayn) on surah 16, verse 106:

﴿Whoever disbelieves in Allah after his belief—except one who is compelled while his heart is firm in faith﴾ (is excepted) in uttering disbelief, so he utters it. ﴿And his heart is at rest with faith.﴾ "Man" (مَن) is either a subject (mubtada') or a conditional particle (shartiyyah), and the predicate (khabar) or the response (jawab) is ﴿for them﴾ a severe threat (wa'id shadid), which is indicated by this. ﴿But whoever opens his breast to disbelief﴾ i.e., opens it and expands it (شَرَحَ, sharaha), in the sense that his soul is content with it (طابَتْ بِهِ نَفْسه, tabat bihi nafsuhu).
That (threat) for them [is] because they preferred the worldly life: they chose it.
﴿Those are the ones whom Allah has sealed upon their hearts, their hearing, and their sights, and they are the heedless.﴾ (They are) heedless of what is intended for them.

Commentary of al-Mahalli & al-Suyuti (Tafsir al-Jalalayn) on surah 16, verse 109:

﴿Lā jaram﴾ (certainly, truly) ﴿annahum fī al-ākhirah hum al-khāsirūn﴾ (that they, in the Hereafter, are the losers) because of their destination to the Fire, which is everlasting for them.

Commentary of al-Mahalli & al-Suyuti (Tafsir al-Jalalayn) on surah 16, verse 110:

﴿Then indeed your Lord, for those who emigrated﴾ to al-Madinah ﴿after they had been tested﴾ (i.e., they were tortured and uttered words of disbelief; in another reading, with the verb in the active voice, i.e., they disbelieved, or they tested the people away from faith) ﴿then struggled and were patient﴾ in obedience ﴿indeed your Lord, after it [i.e., the trial]﴾ ﴿is Forgiving﴾ to them ﴿Merciful﴾ toward them. The predicate of the first "inna" is indicated by the predicate of the second.

Remember the Day when every soul will come pleading for itself (تُجادِل), arguing (تُحاجّ) on its own behalf, concerned with nothing but itself, and that is the Day of Resurrection. ﴿And every soul will be paid in full for what it did, and they will not be wronged﴾ in anything.

Commentary of al-Mahalli & al-Suyuti (Tafsir al-Jalalayn) on surah 16, verse 112:

﴿And Allah presents an example﴾: (it is) substituted for it: ﴿a town﴾, which is Makkah, and what is meant is its people, ﴿that was secure and tranquil﴾ from raids, not attacked, ﴿its provision coming to it abundantly﴾, plentifully, ﴿from every place. Then it denied the favours of Allah﴾ by denying the Prophet (ﷺ), ﴿so Allah made it taste the garment of hunger﴾, so they suffered famine for seven years, ﴿and fear﴾, by the expeditions (sarāyā) of the Prophet (ﷺ).

Commentary of al-Mahalli & al-Suyuti (Tafsir al-Jalalayn) on surah 16, verse 113:

﴿Certainly there came to them a Messenger from among themselves﴾ Muhammad (ﷺ), ﴿but they denied him, so the punishment seized them﴾ the hunger and the fear.

Commentary of al-Mahalli and al-Suyuti (Tafsir al-Jalalayn) on Surah 16, verse 114:

﴿So eat﴾ O believers

"And do not say, concerning what your tongues describe falsely, 'This is lawful and this is unlawful,'" that is, for the description your tongues make of the falsehood, "This is lawful and this is unlawful" — for what Allah has not made lawful nor made unlawful — "so that you may invent falsehood against Allah" by attributing that to Him.
For them is a little enjoyment in this world, and for them in the Hereafter is a painful punishment.

And to those who were Jews We forbade what We have already related to you (ﷺ) earlier, in the verse: ﴿And to those who were Jews We forbade every animal with claws﴾ to the end of it. ﴿And We did not wrong them﴾ by forbidding that, ﴿but they were wronging themselves﴾ by committing the sins that necessitated it.

Commentary of al-Mahalli & al-Suyuti (Tafsir al-Jalalayn) on surah 16, verse 119:

﴿Then indeed your Lord — for those who did evil﴾ (i.e., shirk) ﴿out of ignorance, then repented﴾ (i.e., returned) ﴿after that and made amends﴾ (i.e., their deeds) ﴿indeed your Lord, after it﴾ (i.e., the ignorance or the repentance) ﴿is Oft-Forgiving﴾ (towards them) ﴿Most Merciful﴾ (to them)

Indeed, Ibrahim was an ummah (ummah): an imam (imam), a model to follow, gathering in himself the qualities of goodness. ﴿Devoutly obedient﴾ (qanitan), obeying ﴿Allah﴾, ﴿upright in faith﴾ (hanifan), inclining toward the upright religion.

Commentary of al-Mahalli & al-Suyuti (Tafsir al-Jalalayn) on surah 16, verse 121:

﴿Thankful for His blessings; He chose him﴾ eh, He selected him (اصْطَفاهُ, istafahu, "He chose him").

Commentary of al-Mahalli & al-Suyuti (Tafsir al-Jalalayn) on surah 16, verse 122:

﴿And We gave him⦆ here there is an iltifat (shift) from the third person (ghayba) [i.e., "We gave him" instead of "I gave him" in the first person; the shift is from the third-person address] ﴿in this world a good name⦆, which is the good praise from all the people of the religions ﴿and indeed he, in the Hereafter, is among the righteous﴾ who have the lofty ranks.

Commentary of al-Mahalli & al-Suyuti (Tafsir al-Jalalayn) on surah 16, verse 123:

﴿Then We revealed to you﴾ O Muhammad, ﴿"Follow the creed (millah) of Ibrahim, ḥanīfan (upright, inclining away from falsehood), and he was not among the polytheists"﴾. It is repeated as a refutation of the claim of the Jews and the Christians that they are upon his religion (dīn).

The Commentary of al-Mahalli and al-Suyuti (Tafsir al-Jalalayn) on Surah 16, verse 124:

﴿Indeed, the Sabbath was only made[ (i.e., its) observance obligatory] upon those who differed concerning it﴾ [that is, upon the Prophets' people], and they are the Jews. They were commanded to devote themselves to worship on Friday, but they said: "We do not want it," and they chose the Sabbath, so it was made strict for them concerning it. ﴿Indeed, your Lord will judge between them on the Day of Resurrection concerning that about which they used to differ﴾ [through His command to reward the obedient and punish the disobedient for violating its sanctity].

Commentary of al-Mahalli & al-Suyuti (Tafsir al-Jalalayn) on surah 16, verse 125:

﴿Invite﴾ the people, O Muhammad, ﴿to the way of your Lord﴾, i.e., His religion, ﴿with wisdom﴾, i.e., with the Qur'an, ﴿and good instruction﴾, i.e., its admonitions, or gentle speech. ﴿And argue with them in a manner that is best﴾, i.e., with the argument that is best, such as calling to God through His signs and calling to His proofs. ﴿Indeed, your Lord is most knowing﴾, i.e., He is Knower, ﴿of who has strayed from His way, and He is most knowing of those who are guided﴾, so He will recompense them. This [verse] came before the command to fight, and it was revealed when Hamzah was killed and mutilated, whereupon the Prophet (ﷺ) said, when he saw him: "I will mutilate seventy of them in your place."

**Commentary of al-Mahalli and al-Suyuti (Tafsir al-Jalalayn) (tafsir, meaning exegesis) on surah 16, verse 126:**

﴿If you punish, then punish with the like of that with which you were punished. But if you endure patiently, it is indeed better for those who are patient.﴾ Enduring patiently refrains from retaliation. ﴿It is indeed better for those who are patient﴾, meaning the patience. So the Prophet (ﷺ) refrained, and he made expiation for his oath. Narrated by al-Bazzar.

Commentary of al-Mahalli & al-Suyuti (Tafsir al-Jalalayn) on surah 16, verse 127:

﴿And be patient, and your patience is not except by Allah﴾ by His enabling (tawfiq) ﴿And do not grieve over them﴾ i.e., the disbelievers, if they do not believe, out of your eagerness (hirs) for their faith ﴿And do not be in distress over what they plot﴾ i.e., do not concern yourself with their plotting, for I am your helper against them.

Tafsir al-Jalalayn (al-Mahalli and al-Suyuti) on Surah 16, verse 128:

﴿Indeed, Allah is with those who fear Him﴾ [i.e., who avoid] disbelief (kufr) and sins (ma'asi), ﴿and those who are doers of good﴾ [i.e., who do good] through obedience (ta'a) and patience (sabr), [He is with them] by aid (awn) and victory (nasr).
